demo_lead_1: DEMS checks public weather, air quality, river, earthquake and global disaster data near you.
demo_lead_2: It turns all of that into one level: Safe, Watch or Warning.
demo_lead_3: It shows you the nearest shelter and a way there that steers around danger.
demo_honest: A student project. Levels are estimates from public data, not official warnings. Shelters are sample data. The video is an illustration; the live app shows real conditions.
demo_role_citizen_body: See your level, the hazard map, shelters and a safe route. Pack a go-bag. Report an incident.
demo_role_volunteer_body: Check and update incident reports from the field.
demo_role_admin_body: Manage shelters and reports, and send alerts.
demo_hood_intro: For teachers and the curious: how DEMS is built.
demo_hood_arch_body: One SvelteKit app does both the screens and the server API, written in TypeScript. It runs on Vercel in Tokyo, close to Thailand. Data lives in Supabase, a hosted Postgres database, also in Tokyo.
demo_hood_flow_body: DEMS asks public sources for conditions near you, compares each value with published thresholds and gives every hazard a level. The worst live hazard sets your level. If no source answers, the level is Unknown, never Safe, and data older than 3 hours turns Unknown too. In Sweden, SMHI's official warnings set the weather level.
demo_hood_db_body: Row-level security in Postgres controls who can read or change each table. Staff sign in with a role, volunteer or admin. Reports and route requests are rate-limited per connection. Secret keys stay on the server, and every database call gives up after 8 seconds with a clear message instead of hanging.
demo_hood_tests_body: Over 100 unit tests (Vitest) check the level rules, routing, go-bag lists and translations. Over 70 browser tests (Playwright) tap through every screen on a simulated phone with all outside services mocked, and run automatic accessibility checks (axe) against WCAG AA.
demo_hood_data_body: Real: weather, air quality and river forecasts (Open-Meteo), earthquakes (USGS), global disaster alerts (GDACS), the map (OpenStreetMap) and routes (openrouteservice). Sample: shelters, past disasters and evacuation routes in our own database. Sample records are labelled and never change your level.
demo_hood_history_body: DEMS started as an Express server with a MySQL database and a separate front end. It was rebuilt as one SvelteKit app on Supabase, so the screens and the API share one codebase, the database enforces its own access rules, and hosting is free and close to Thailand. The citizen screens were then redesigned for clarity, with a dark, high-contrast look.
map_scope: The map shows the whole region. Your level only counts hazards near you.
shelters_th_note: Example shelters: Thailand has no public shelter list. In a real emergency, follow DDPM and local announcements.
shelters_dev_body: Myanmar has no public shelter list we can use yet. In an emergency, follow official and local announcements.
shelters_se_body: Sweden has about 64,000 civil-defence shelters for war and air raids. For storms or floods, follow SMHI and your municipality. MCF (formerly MSB) keeps the official map.
